# Privacy spec — what leaves the machine

This page is generated from the code that enforces it, not written beside it.
The shipped collector runs data mode `metadata`
(`DEFAULT_POLICY.version = 2026-05-17.metadata-v1`, `packages/shared/src/policy.ts`).
Managed or upload-enabled installs are locked to that mode; see
[ADR-0004](architecture/0004-managed-metadata-only-privacy.md).

## The four buckets

| Bucket | Rule (derived, mechanical) | Source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| Suppressed before local write | Any captured payload key matching `forbiddenRawContentFieldNames` is removed before the local database write in every supported mode; only its field name survives as a receipt. | `forbiddenRawContentFieldNames` in `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts` |
| Never collected — no mode | Forbidden field names outside `rawContentCategorySchema`: even a hypothetical evidence-mode policy admits only the enum's categories via `evidence.allowedCategories`, so nothing outside them can ever be admitted. | computed: `forbiddenRawContentFieldNames\rawContentCategorySchema` |
| Collected hashed | Captured payload keys matching `protectedMetadataFieldNames` have their value replaced by a truncated SHA-256 (`sha256:` + 16 hex chars) before persistence. | `protectedMetadataFieldNames`, `hashProtectedValue` in `packages/shared/src/policy.ts` |
| Collected plain (typed envelope) | The typed fields of the upload payload schema cross the boundary as-is, validated by the outbound sealer. | `aiWorkIngestBatchSchema`, `aiInteractionEventSchema` in `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts` |

## Never collected — not admittable in any mode

Computed as the forbidden names that are not among the
`rawContentCategorySchema` categories (`prompt`, `output`, `tool_input`, `tool_output`, `command_body`, `file_body`, `api_body`)
— the only values `policyConfigSchema.evidence.allowedCategories` accepts.

## Collected hashed

Any captured payload key matching one of these names has its value replaced
by `hashProtectedValue`: `sha256:` + the first 16 hex characters of the
SHA-256 digest. Example (deterministic):

    hashProtectedValue("sentinel-actor@example.test")
    → "sha256:0f5b0302438e5ba7"

## Collected plain — upload envelope

The upload payload shape is `aiWorkIngestBatchSchema`
(`packages/shared/src/schemas.ts`). Envelope fields:

1. `tenantId` — string, optional
2. `installKey` — string, required
3. `appVersion` — string, optional
4. `events` — array<object> (length ≥ 1, ≤ 500), required

Each `events[i]` wraps an `aiInteractionEventSchema` object plus a
`suppressedFields` receipt list (bounded ASCII field
names only). Typed event fields:

1. `id` — string, required.
2. `sessionId` — string, optional.
3. `tenantId` — string, optional.
4. `actorId` — string, optional — normalized name also appears in `protectedMetadataFieldNames`; inside free-form metadata such keys are value-hashed (see *Collected hashed*), and as a typed field it crosses under the outbound identifier contract.
5. `source` — enum(anthropic_admin | anthropic_usage | claude_code | codex | github | openai_usage | vendor_import | manual | unknown), required.
6. `dataMode` — enum(metadata | event_detail | evidence), optional.
7. `eventType` — enum(session_start | session_stop | user_prompt_submit | assistant_response | tool_use | tool_result | otel_span | usage_rollout | usage_transcript | usage_vendor_import | unknown), required.
8. `observedAt` — string, required.
9. `model` — string, optional.
10. `projectKey` — string, optional.
11. `customerKey` — string, optional.
12. `workflowKey` — string, optional.
13. `intent` — enum(customer | project | workflow | internal | overhead | unknown), optional.
14. `actionClass` — enum(continue | validate | test | edit | read | write | shell | mcp | browser | review | other), optional.
15. `inputTokens` — number, optional.
16. `outputTokens` — number, optional.
17. `cacheReadTokens` — number, optional.
18. `cacheCreationTokens` — number, optional.
19. `costUsd` — number, optional.
20. `metadata` — record(string, unknown), optional.

Free-form `metadata` crosses only when the outbound sealer admits each key;
unknown keys default to local-only.
